extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, number theorists, and developers evaluating or using PARI/GP
extracted.subtask_description: Identify and assess the features, strengths, and capabilities of the PARI/GP computer algebra system, especially for number-theory computations and embedding in other applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speed / high performance
rubrics_metrics.description: The PARI/GP system is capable of doing formal computations on recursive types at high speed; one of its three main strengths is its speed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show timing output for operations (e.g., factorial and complex exponentiation). gp2c-compiled scripts typically run three to four times faster; compiling PARI/GP with GMP provides faster computations than the native kernel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data types familiar to mathematicians
rubrics_metrics.description: Possibility of directly using data types that are familiar to mathematicians is cited as a main strength.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PARI/GP supports data types such as matrices, polynomials, power series, algebraic numbers, and special functions which align with mathematical practice and facilitate usage by mathematicians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensive algebraic number theory module
rubrics_metrics.description: PARI/GP includes an extensive algebraic number theory module; it is primarily aimed at number theorists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides high-level number-theory-specific functionality like bnfinit for number fields and tools to inspect class numbers (example: K = bnfinit(x^2 + 23); K.cyc).

rubrics_metrics.name: Arbitrary precision arithmetic
rubrics_metrics.description: PARI/GP performs arbitrary precision calculations; the significand can be millions of digits long (and billions on 64-bit machines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precision is adjustable (example: \p 212 yields realprecision = 221 significant digits). Use GMP to improve performance of arbitrary-precision operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integer factorization capability
rubrics_metrics.description: It can compute factorizations (integer factorization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example usage: factor(2^z-1) in a loop producing factor lists; timings are provided to illustrate performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elliptic curve computations
rubrics_metrics.description: PARI/GP can perform elliptic curve computations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among core computational capabilities relevant to number theory; no explicit examples on the page but included as a primary feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: General algebraic number theory calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Capability to perform algebraic number theory calculations beyond basic operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions like bnfinit and access to invariants (e.g., class group data) are provided; the system targets deep number-theory tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix, polynomial, and power series handling
rubrics_metrics.description: PARI/GP allows computations with matrices, polynomials, and power series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These data types are explicitly supported and integrated into the system for symbolic and numeric computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algebraic numbers support
rubrics_metrics.description: PARI/GP supports computations with algebraic numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the native data-type support useful for algebraic number theory and symbolic manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special functions implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: PARI/GP implements many special functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for analytic computations; these are available as built-in functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Built-in plotting capability
rubrics_metrics.description: PARI/GP comes with its own built-in graphical plotting capability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides simple visualization directly from gp without needing external plotting tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbolic manipulation capability
rubrics_metrics.description: PARI/GP has some symbolic manipulation capability, e.g., multivariate polynomial and rational function handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbolic features are limited compared to full CASes focused on symbolic algebra, but include common polynomial/rational operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal integration and differentiation
rubrics_metrics.description: PARI/GP has some formal integration and differentiation capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are available but are described as 'some' capability, implying limited symbolic integration compared with specialized CAS.

rubrics_metrics.name: gp interactive command-line interface (usability)
rubrics_metrics.description: gp is an easy-to-use interactive command line interface giving access to PARI functions; it functions as a programmable calculator and contains most control instructions of a standard language like C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: gp is intended for interactive use and scripting; examples show prompt usage and immediate results with timing feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: GP scripting language
rubrics_metrics.description: GP is the name of gp's scripting language which can be used to program gp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GP scripts can be run interactively or compiled via gp2c for performance improvements; the language contains standard control structures resembling C.

rubrics_metrics.name: gp2c compiler (GP-to-C)
rubrics_metrics.description: gp2c compiles GP scripts into C and transparently loads resulting functions into gp; gp2c-understands almost all of GP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compiled gp2c scripts typically run three to four times faster than uncompiled GP code, offering a practical optimization path for heavy computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PARI as a C library (embeddability)
rubrics_metrics.description: PARI is a C library allowing for fast computations and can be called from high-level language applications (C, C++, Pascal, Fortran, Perl, Python).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This makes PARI suitable for embedding in other software projects and for use as a backend computational engine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional GMP linkage for improved performance
rubrics_metrics.description: PARI/GP can be compiled with GMP (GNU Multiple Precision Arithmetic Library) providing faster computations than PARI/GP's native arbitrary-precision kernel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Building with GMP is a recommended performance optimization on systems where GMP is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-platform support
rubrics_metrics.description: It runs on most common operating systems and is cross-platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability across platforms increases accessibility for users on different systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: License / open-source status
rubrics_metrics.description: Versions 2.1.0 and higher are distributed under the GNU General Public License.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GPL licensing implies freedom to use, modify, and redistribute under GPL terms; relevant for adoption and integration policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience suitability (aimed at number theorists)
rubrics_metrics.description: PARI/GP is primarily aimed at number theorists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users whose work focuses on number theory will find domain-specific tools and modules; others may prefer CASes with broader symbolic capabilities.
